Subject: Technical response: KMS/HSM, key residency, and routing options

Anna / Rafael — quick summary of the technical controls and implementation options. Details in the attached spreadsheet (Redwood_DPF_KMS_Response.xlsx). Key points: 

1) Customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM):
   - Hosted API: supported via customer-managed KMS integration (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) for encrypting at-rest model caches and customer data blobs. We offer two modes:
     a) Envelope keys (recommended): Customer KMS holds the envelope key; Redwood manages data keys ephemeral and encrypted under the customer envelope key.
     b) HSM-backed retrievals for high-sensitivity tenants: we support bring-your-own-HSM (PKCS#11) integration for Dedicated and Private deployments.
   - Dedicated/Private: customers can provide HSM endpoints or bring their own KMS to ensure key material never leaves their control plane. For on-prem, keys never leave the air-gapped environment unless explicitly exported by the customer.

2) Key residency and logging:
   - Keys are stored in the region of the customer's KMS. For hosted customers who use Redwood-managed keys, default region is EU (e.g., eu-west-1) if the account is EU-scoped.
   - All KMS operations (Encrypt/Decrypt/Sign) are logged to our audit trail with key-ids, timestamps, and caller identity. We can provide Key Usage reports on a monthly or on-demand basis.

3) Model/request routing and EU-only constraints:
   - Policy-based routing: requests can be routed by policy (region, latency, tenant attribute). You can require EU-only routing for entire tenant or for specific routes.
   - Fallback behavior: we support strict (no fallback) and graceful (fallback to compatible EU-hosted model variant) policies. Fallback to non-EU regions is opt-in and only occurs if explicitly allowed in the routing policy.
   - Auditing: routing decisions are recorded in the trace logs (request_id -> selected cluster). We can export routing audit logs for the retention window you require.

4) Operational artifacts we can provide: KMS integration runbook, HSM onboarding checklist, routing policy examples, and audit log extracts.

Attachments: Redwood_DPF_KMS_Response.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Let me know if you want a short technical call to run through any of the above.

—David Kim
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposed DPA annex language and SCC / DPF approach

Anna — attaching a draft DPA annex (DPA_Annex_Draft_SalviaBank.docx) and below are the key clauses we propose. This is intended for your legal review and should be compatible with SCCs + DPF controls.

- Transfer basis: primary mechanism is EU SCCs for processor transfers. We include a supplemental technical and organizational measures (TOMs) exhibit that references Redwood's DPF controls (encryption, routing, KMS integration, contractual subprocessor limits).

- KMS/HSM clause: customer-managed keys are expressly permitted; Redwood acknowledges that key material provided by customer remains customer property. For Hosted, we include a data flow description and a commitment to never export key material from the EU region for EU-scoped tenants.

- Model routing and fallback: the annex allows customers to set routing constraints. By default, we include a strict-routing option (no cross-border fallback) and a fallback option that will only activate with explicit customer authorization. Audit logs must be made available on request for compliance checks.

- Right to audit / evidence: Redwood will provide evidentiary artifacts (KMS runbook, routing audit logs, SOC2 report excerpts) under standard NDA and evidence-sharing procedures.

If this aligns with your expectations, we can tighten language and track redlines.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
